learning_outcomes.text: Student knows basic social theories of tourism and understands the contemporary transformations taking place in the field of tourism.
Student can analyze changes in motivations for tourism and identify factors influencing its contemporary character.
Student has a need to independently develop their competencies regarding changing trends in tourism.
Student respects diversity and appreciates the importance of human rights in contact with other cultures.

syllabus_topics: Tourism as a subject of sociological research, sociological theory of tourism. Travel and tourism, real and metaphorical travel. Transformations and development of tourism, state policy in the field of tourism, motivations for tourism.
Functions and dysfunctions of tourism in contemporary society. Leisure and the development of tourism, Poles' leisure time and recreational trips.

Methodology of research in sociology of tourism: general methodology of sciences and specific methodologies, basic paradigms of specific sciences, positivist approach, interpretive (humanistic) approach, methods and techniques used in tourism sociology research.

Traveling in social theories: travel as contact with otherness (Georg Simmel, Alfred Schutz, Florian Znaniecki, Robert Merton, Bernhard Waldenfels, Tzvetan Todorov); travel as a form of cultural contact (Theron Nuñez, Geert Hofstede), tourism as a form of colonialism (Louis Turner, John Ash and Dennison Nash), semiotics of travel (Dean MacCannell), travel as consumption, social roles of the traveler, McDisneyization of post-tourism (George Ritzer).

Sociological analysis of the tourism market: domestic and international tourist traffic, types of tourist traffic and forms of tourism (mass, active, alternative, qualified, unconventional agritourism). Forms of tourism in contemporary Western society - business tourism, ethnic-national, social, religious-pilgrimage, sightseeing, health, agritourism, weekend tourism, cultural, sex tourism, "trauma tourism".

Cultural tourism (culture and tourism, cultural heritage, world cultural heritage, World Heritage List, cultural heritage and tourism). Forms of cultural tourism - including slow tourism, thanatourism, literary tourism, esoteric tourism, culinary tourism, geocaching and others.
History as a tourist experience: tourist adaptations of cultural heritage, tourism and local communities and governments, architecture and tourism, postmodern museums.

The problem of authenticity: cold and hot authenticity, historical souvenirs, ethnic souvenirs, material objects, selling and buying cultural authenticity, spectacle, authenticity of experience. Experiencing history in the museum.
Religious tourism in contemporary religions, the phenomenon of pilgrimage in Poland.
Qualified and unconventional tourism: consumers in the tourism services market, using the example of motorcycle tourism in Poland, experiencing place and culture based on research on backpacking.
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes are verified by test results. Students participate in classes, getting acquainted with the teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the consent of the lecturer.
